chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Ben Webster's gambling temper and pool
summary: Webster lost at cards, races and pool, got angry with his cue-ball eyes, and the Roseland dressing-room players stopped gambling with him; he was the life of the party.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Even in Fletcher's band, you know, during the breaks in The Roseland when they had -- they had two band-stands there all the time. Well, they would play half hour house sets, something. Fletcher's band would take a break, and they had a dressing room downstairs, and the guys would play cards and all these things. They played 21, you know, everything else, you know, and they played for money, you know.

So Ben would always lose. He'd always -- I don't remember having ever, ever known him to win a huge sum of money; even when he would go out and play the races, he'd lose. He'd get mad at the horses. He'd stomp his feet and all this stuff, but he'd get over it quick, you know. He didn't mean anything. He just had a temper, you know? And that was the only time he'd show it. He was a hard to loser, and it got so the guys didn't want to gamble with him anymore, and that made him mad, you know.
He said, 'What am I, an outcast or something? You guys -- he wanted to say this or something -- the guys would say, 'Well, we're only playing whist, man, this is, you know --'
-- We're not gambling or anything, just pass the time. Well, come on, let's start here blackjack. Let's do something.

He was the life of the party, you know, but that was Ben Webster, you know -- Kansas City and all down that way. He was a good pool player. He could shoot pool. He wanted to gamble in pool. He wanted to bet on the eight ball and all this stuff. And from any outside observer that didn't know Ben Webster, you'd think he was a gambler, you know, to hear him talk, you know. You'd think he was anything but that great saxophonist that he really was. He just passed recently and -- but it's -- we lost another
